brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.requirement: Shelf unit for books (a storage structure with a flat top surface to shelve books on)
requirements.evidence: Three hex bases (piece:-1,0,0 half-s, piece:0,0,0 full, piece:1,0,0 half-n) joined in a row by joint bolts, with covers on the top faces forming a 441 x 144 mm deck (cover:-1,0,0, cover:0,0,0, cover:1,0,0). A book-stack prop sits on that deck. check_build is ok, meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only; it has no load rating or structural analysis. Nothing in the build verifies 50 kg, and the printed material and joint strength are not something I can see. The build uses joint bolts and covers, but that does not establish the rating.

Two drawers: drawer:0#-1,0#cut (style n, on the cut face of half-s base at q=-1) and drawer:0#1,0#cut (style s, on the cut face of half-n base at q=1). Both are placed and check_build reports no drawer issues.

finish.summary: Built a three-base hex shelf (half, full, half) with joint bolts, a top cover deck carrying a book stack prop, and two drawers on the cut faces of the two half bases. Layout and drawers pass check_build with meshClash clear. The 50 kg load rating cannot be verified in the configurator and is reported as unmet.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
